# Sensor Market

## Overview
This wiki page provides an overview of the competitive landscape for the sensor market in Q3 2026, based on internal [Aurora Labs](./aurora-labs.md) [documentation](./documentation.md) authored by Jonah Park. It evaluates key garden and soil sensor vendors, adjacent kitchen and lifestyle products, and outlines strategic battlecard updates.

## Key Details
The competitive landscape is categorized by sensor applications, notably garden/soil [sensors](./sensors.md) and adjacent lifestyle products.

### Garden / Soil Sensors
* **Aurora Labs ([Nova Widget](./nova-widget.md)):** Utilizes [MeshSync protocol](./meshsync-protocol.md) with optional cloud connectivity, features IP54 [waterproofing](./waterproofing.md), and is powered by a CR2032 battery.
* **[SenseNode](./sensenode.md) ([SN-400](./sensenode.md)):** Utilizes [LoRaWAN](./lorawan.md) protocol with required cloud connectivity, features IP67 waterproofing, and is powered by a CR2450 battery.
* **CheapoCo (SoilStick):** Utilizes WiFi with required cloud connectivity, lacks waterproofing (none), and is powered via USB.

### Kitchen / Lifestyle (Adjacent)
* **[TeaBuddy](./teabuddy.md) ([Puck](./teabuddy.md)):** Operates on [BLE](./ble.md) as a local-only tea timer. Viewed as a partnership or co-[marketing](./marketing.md) opportunity rather than a direct competitor.
* **TimerCap (KS failed 2024):** A mechanical, non-smart product.

### Battlecard Updates & Strategy
* **SenseNode Strategy:** Emphasize the long-term subscription cost over a 3-year period when competing against SenseNode.
* **TeaBuddy Strategy:** Pursue partnership and co-marketing opportunities rather than treating them as competitors.
